reviewer.name: Claude Sonnet, fresh subagent (cold reader 1)
reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-25 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session), round 2

evidence: Draft is one inserted sentence, nothing replaced (SOURCE.txt): "And a community’s autonomy doesn’t let it take away rights a person can’t sign away, or make the law outside disappear." His line: "But autonomy is not permission to erase non-waivable individual rights, and it does not make outside jurisdiction disappear." Meaning: both halves of his limit are there. "erase non-waivable individual rights" became "take away rights a person can’t sign away" (same sense, plain words); "does not make outside jurisdiction disappear" became "make the law outside disappear" (jurisdiction softened to law, but the same point for a lay reader, and the paragraph's own "courts, regulatory agencies" carries it). "But" became "And", which is right here because nothing before it praises autonomy to contrast with. "a community’s" only names whose autonomy his line means in an essay on communities. No new claim, name, number or first-person fact. In context it sits at the end of the "outside" paragraph after "The key is that it’s not the same people." and reads as the counterweight to "Note that 'outside' doesn’t have to mean the nation-state": outside needn't be the state, but a community's autonomy still doesn't remove the outside law; its first half also ties back to paragraph two's "What protections will there be for the person’s interests" and "This power to remove people is so easily abused". Pronoun: "it" is the community (autonomy cannot sensibly take rights away); "autonomy" is the head noun so a first glance could hesitate, but meaning resolves it at once, so not a fault. Tells: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 and found no row PRESENT. Looked hardest at T03 ("autonomy" first appears here, but the section's abuse-of-removal and outside-help thread sets it up, and it is his point, not a ledger insertion), T17 (a stated limit in plain words, not an aphorism; his own wording is the more aphoristic one), T21 (two coordinated limits mirror his own pair and do one job), T20/T29 (it ends the paragraph but adds a new consideration, and replaces the shorter polished closer "The key is..." as the last line), T26 ("outside" recurs, but as the paragraph's subject and a deliberate callback to its quoted "outside"), T16/T22 (no "not X, it's Y", no coaching). C02 fine, C03 and C04 nothing added. Linter finding "D9 follows the source order": for a single inserted sentence, "1/1 paragraphs follow the source's points in its order" is vacuous; I checked its pointers T13 (the sentence notices something: the callback to "outside" and the earlier protections question) and T09 (it is not equalized with its neighbours; it is the one place the paragraph turns to rights and law), both absent. Accepted.
